The paid platform had hosted sensitive personal information of 168 people aboard the presidential jet during President Lee Jae Myung’s trip to Europe in June. Those affected included not only the president and first lady but also high-ranking officials, including then-chief of staff for policy Kim Yong-beom, National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac, current Prime Minister Han Seong-sook and several Cabinet members, as well as senior officials from Cheong Wa Dae and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, security personnel and reporters traveling with the presidential delegation. VirusTotal, a web service owned by Google, scans uploaded files and URLs simultaneously using more than 70 antivirus engines and security tools. items.title: 3 in 4 Seoul residents drink tap water: survey
items.title_zh: 首尔四分之三的居民饮用自来水：调查
items.summary: Three in four Seoul residents now drink the city’s tap water, which is sold under the brand name Arisu, and more of them are drinking it away from home, a city survey showed Thursday. In the Seoul Metropolitan Government’s annual survey, 75.5 percent of residents said they drank tap water this year. That was up from 75 percent last year and 69.6 percent in 2024, when the city started using its own measure. The figure adds the 53.9 percent who drink tap water at home to the 21.6 percent who drink it only outside the home. The city created the measure because standards for calculating tap water drinking rates vary by country and institution. Under the American Water Works Association’s criteria, Seoul’s rate was 78.2 percent, 13.2 percentage points above the U.S. figure of 65 percent in 2024. Paris counts people who drink tap water either alone or along with other water. By that method, Seoul’s rate was 82.5 percent, compared with 81 percent for the French capital in 2025. items.title: Multicultural marriages in Korea edge down in 2025
items.title_zh: 韩国的多元文化婚姻在2025年逐渐减少
items.summary: The number of multicultural marriages in Korea edged down in 2025 from a year earlier, data showed Thursday, taking up 8.9 percent of all marriages. The country recorded 21,399 multicultural marriages last year, down 0.2 percent, or 51, from 21,450 in 2024, according to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Marriages involving foreign wives accounted for 71.4 percent of multicultural marriages, followed by those with foreign husbands at 18.9 percent and those with naturalized citizens at 9.7 percent. The average age for first marriages was 37.1 years for husbands and 29.7 years for wives. Husbands were older than their wives in 75.2 percent of multicultural marriages. In 36.1 percent of all multicultural marriages, the husband was at least 10 years older than his wife. Vietnamese wives accounted for 25.3 percent of all multicultural marriages, followed by Chinese wives at 15.1 percent and Thai wives at 9.2 percent. items.summary: The foreign ministry failed to raise the travel alert for Cambodia or take other necessary measures in a timely manner, even though it had been aware that job scams targeting South Koreans were worsening in the Southeast Asian nation, the state audit agency said Thursday. Such crimes sparked public outrage last year after a South Korean college student was tortured to death by a Chinese scam ring in Cambodia, shedding light on a series of similar cases where young South Koreans were lured into the country with promises of high-paying jobs only to end up being kidnapped. According to the Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI), the foreign ministry learned after December 2023 through information from overseas diplomatic missions and private firms that South Koreans were falling victim to job scams and kidnapping in Cambodia, with the nature of the crimes becoming increasingly brutal. At that time, Kwon had stressed that a long-term joint investigation team would be necessary "as long as the capabilities and will of the insurrection forces remain as they were." items.summary: More than 470,000 personal data records have been leaked from 37 companies across the financial sector over the past month, with the amount of funds stolen estimated at 1 billion won ($745,000), the financial regulator said Thursday. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) held a meeting with officials from financial trade associations and government agencies, including the Financial Supervisory Service and the Financial Security Institute, to review data protection systems and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities in the financial sector. Since Sept. 30, when the first data leak was detected, a total of 40 data leak incidents have been reported at 37 companies, including four commercial banks, five financial investment firms, three insurance firms and five savings banks, according to the FSC. The regulator said the leaked data did not include sensitive personal information that could be used for illegal financial transactions, such as customers' names, national identification numbers or bank account numbers. The move sparks concerns it could draw Korea into the war between Iran and the United States. The expansion proposal passed a vice ministerial meeting Thursday morning. After Cabinet and presidential approval, the motion will go to the National Assembly for final authorization. Under the proposal, the unit’s personnel ceiling would rise from 320 to 395, with the addition of a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, an explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team and unmanned mine-clearing equipment. The additional 75 personnel would include 45 assigned to the P-8 aircraft and 30 to the EOD team. The new equipment would include unmanned surface and underwater vehicles and remotely operated underwater robots. items.title: Saudi Arabia signs $403 million development loan agreements to support Syria's reconstruction
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯签署4.03亿美元发展贷款协议支持叙利亚重建
items.summary: RIYADH — The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) signed six concessional development loan agreements worth more than $403 million with Syria on Thursday to support key sectors, including energy, water, health, housing, infrastructure and digital transformation.The agreements were signed in the presence of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman and Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa, in implementation of the directives of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the Crown Prince.SFD Chief Executive Officer Sultan Al-Marshad and Syrian Minister of Finance Mohammed Yisr Barnieh signed the agreements, which aim to restore essential services, rehabilitate damaged infrastructure and improve living conditions across Syria.The agreements cover six development projects targeting critical infrastructure and public services.A $90 million project will rehabilitate generating units at the Aleppo Thermal Power Plant, benefiting approximately five million people.The project aims to restore the plant's electricity generation capacity, provide a stable power supply to residents and public facilities, support economic and industrial activity, and strengthen the national electricity grid.Another agreement, valued at $30 million, will support the modernization of Syria's drinking water metering system through the supply and installation of 300,000 smart water meters.The project is expected to benefit approximately 1.5 million people across several governorates while improving the quality and efficiency of water services.A $105 million project will finance the construction, rehabilitation and equipping of 25 civil defense centers across several governorates, benefiting more than seven million people.The initiative seeks to strengthen emergency response and disaster management capabilities, including debris removal and management, while supporting stability in communities affected by the conflict.The agreements also include a $60 million housing rehabilitation project targeting up to 10,000 damaged residential units in various parts of Syria, contributing to improved living conditions and social stability.In the healthcare sector, a $100 million project will support the rehabilitation, construction and equipping of hospitals and health centers.The project aims to restore essential and specialized medical services, upgrade priority healthcare facilities, expand access to treatment and reduce pressure on existing hospitals.Additionally, more than $18 million will be allocated to support the digital transformation and institutional development of the Syrian Ministry of Finance.The project will introduce an integrated digital system designed to improve the experience of beneficiaries and enhance the efficiency and transparency of government financial services.The agreements reflect Saudi Arabia's continued development support for Syria through SFD, focusing on restoring essential services, rebuilding infrastructure and improving access to sustainable public services.In September 2025, Saudi Arabia, through SFD, provided two grants to Syria to supply crude oil and cover part of government employees' salaries for three months.

items.title: Hajj and Umrah Committee reviews early pilgrimage preparations

items.summary: JEDDAH — The Permanent Committee for Hajj and Umrah meeting reviewed the latest developments in early preparations for the Hajj 2027 and ongoing development projects designed to facilitate the pilgrims' journey. Deputy Emir of Makkah Prince Saud bin Mishaal chaired the meeting, which discussed the ongoing Umrah season and preparations for the Hajj 2027.The meeting was held in line with the directives of Advisor to Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, Emir of Makkah and Chairman of the Permanent Committee for Hajj and Umrah Prince Khalid Al-Faisal. During the meeting, the committee reviewed the efforts of relevant entities serving Umrah pilgrims. These efforts aimed to provide all necessary facilities for visitors to the Grand Mosque and enable them to perform their rituals in ease and comfort. The committee also reviewed operations at King Abdulaziz International Airport and its readiness to serve 65 million passengers annually. The meeting examined the range of services provided to pilgrims, including check-in and processing platforms, health centers, air-conditioned rest areas, and welcome halls. The committee reviewed the latest developments in early preparations for this year's Hajj and ongoing development projects designed to facilitate the pilgrims' journey. The meeting also discussed several items on its agenda and adopted the necessary recommendations.

items.title: Saudi interior minister meets Bulgaria’s president and PM in Sofia

items.summary: SOFIA — Saudi Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif met with President of Bulgaria Iliana Iotova in the capital Sofia on Wednesday. This is in line with the directives of the Saudi leadership. During the meeting, the interior minister conveyed the greetings of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, along with their wishes for continued progress and prosperity for Bulgaria and its people. He also congratulated Iotova on her victory in the presidential election.Prince Abdulaziz also met with Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev. At the start of the meeting, the minister conveyed the greetings of the Crown Prince to Radev, along with his wishes for continued progress and prosperity for the Bulgarian people.Both the Bulgarian president and prime minister condemned the attacks against Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthi militia and affirmed Bulgaria’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia. The meetings reviewed bilateral relations between the two friendly countries and addressed several issues, including ways to strengthen their ongoing security cooperation.

items.title: Saudi Crown Prince, Syrian President call for urgent regional de-escalation
items.title_zh: 沙特王储、叙利亚总统呼吁紧急缓和地区紧张局势
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa in Riyadh on Wednesday. During their official talks, the Crown Prince and Al-Sharaa underscored the urgent imperative of galvanizing and intensifying regional and international efforts to defuse tensions, avert further escalation and contain mounting crises, while reaffirming the primacy of dialogue and diplomacy and the pursuit of peaceful solutions to disputes. **media[2789963]** The leaders stressed the imperative of an immediate cessation of all actions that jeopardize the security of maritime navigation and waterways in the Red Sea, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and the Strait of Hormuz. They reviewed the close bilateral relations between the two countries and explored avenues for further advancing and strengthening cooperation across all fields. **media[2789965]** The leaders also exchanged views on the prevailing regional and international developments, including the grave repercussions that any military escalation could have on regional and international security and stability, the safety of international navigation, the continuity of energy supplies, and the stability of the global economy. The Crown Prince and the Syrian president commended the significant convergence of their positions and perspectives on regional and international issues of mutual interest, underscoring the depth of coordination and consultation between the two countries. **media[2789964]** At the outset of their talks, the Crown Prince conveyed to Al-Sharaa the greetings of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman, along with his sincere wishes for his continued health and well-being, and for further progress and prosperity for Syria and its people. On his part, Al-Sharaa reciprocated his greetings and heartfelt wishes to King Salman for his continued health and well-being, and further growth and prosperity for the Saudi people. During the session, a memorandum of understanding on industrial cooperation was signed between the Saudi Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and the Syrian Ministry of Industry, Internal Trade and Consumer Protection. An agreement on cooperation between the defense ministries of the two countries was also signed, alongside two memoranda of understanding on cooperation in agriculture and environmental protection between the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture and the Syrian Ministries of Local Administration and Environment, and Agriculture. In addition, several agreements were concluded between the Saudi Fund for Development and the Syrian side, covering a range of projects in infrastructure, healthcare, housing, and financial services. Al-Sharaa had arrived in Riyadh earlier on Wednesday on an official visit in response to an invitation from King Salman. Upon arrival at King Khalid International Airport, Al-Sharaa was received by Deputy Emir of Riyadh Prince Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Riyadh Mayor Prince Faisal bin Abdulaziz bin Ayyaf, and Minister of Transport and Logistics Saleh Al-Jasser, the accompanying minister. The Syrian president was accompanied by high-ranking officials, including the ministers of defense, foreign, finance, and industry.

items.title: Al-Samaani underscores Supreme Court’s pivotal role in safeguarding judicial consistency
items.title_zh: Al-Samaani强调最高法院在保障司法一致性方面的关键作用
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Justice Dr. Walid Al-Samaani underscored the Supreme Court’s pivotal role in safeguarding the consistency of judicial principles and rulings, ensuring the sound application of Islamic Shariah and applicable laws, and reinforcing the quality, integrity, and reliability of judicial proceedings. He made the remarks during a meeting with Sheikh Dr. Khalid Al-Luhaidan, president of the Supreme Court, and members of the court. The minister affirmed that progress in the justice sector has been achieved, by the grace of God, through the unlimited support of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the continued support and close follow-up of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman. Al-Samaani commended the efforts of the president and members of the Supreme Court and the progress achieved in judicial performance. He also expressed appreciation for their commitment to training and professional development, participation in workshops, and contributions through feedback and proposals for improvement. The minister noted that the Supreme Court, as a court of law, plays a central role in maintaining the stability of judicial principles and decisions. He stressed the importance of adhering to established judicial principles and enhancing the quality of judgments and their legal reasoning. Al-Samaani also emphasized the importance of implementing the Rules Governing the Work of Technical Offices, strengthening the preparation and technical review of judicial studies and draft judgments, and expanding the adoption of artificial intelligence applications to support judicial work and improve the quality of judicial studies and judgments. He encouraged Court members to contribute their views and development proposals, supporting greater institutional maturity and judicial quality.

items.title: Several new Public Security services launched on Absher
items.title_zh: 在Absher上推出几项新的公安服务
items.summary: RIYADH — Director of Public Security Lt. Gen. Mohammed Al-Bassami on Wednesday launched several new Public Security services through the Ministry of Interior’s electronic platform ‘Absher,’ at a ceremony held at the General Directorate of Public Security in Riyadh. The ceremony was held under the patronage of Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif. The new services introduced on the Absher Individuals platform include bidding on motorcycle license plates through the individual auction service, printing driving licenses, replacing previously issued Saudi driving licenses for residents, and a range of air rifle licensing services such as issuing and renewing licenses, transferring ownership, issuing replacements for lost or damaged licenses, and printing licenses. The launch also featured several new services on the Absher Business platform, including accident notifications, license plate replacement for establishments, registration of used vehicles, transfer of ownership of used vehicles to a main establishment, printing vehicle registration documents following ownership transfers, and obtaining permits to hold fireworks displays. The introduction of these services is part of the Ministry of Interior’s ongoing efforts to advance digital transformation and enhance the quality of electronic services, thereby improving beneficiary satisfaction among citizens, residents, and visitors. These automated services are designed to save time and effort while eliminating the need to visit the ministry’s departments in person.

items.title: Commerce ministry warns businesses against misuse of establishment bank accounts
items.title_zh: 商务部警告企业不要滥用机构银行账户
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Commerce has warned business owners against any unlawful activity conducted through their establishments’ bank accounts. It emphasized the importance of monitoring all financial transactions and transfers and preventing others from exploiting these accounts for practices that violate regulations. The ministry indicated that an establishment’s bank account is intended solely for its commercial activities. It added that owners must be fully aware of all contracts, agreements, transactions, and financial transfers involving their establishments and monitor them continuously to avoid being held accountable for any violations or crimes committed through their accounts. The ministry said irregular transactions involving an establishment’s bank account may include receiving cash deposits or transfers from unknown parties; sending funds domestically or internationally to individuals or entities with no contractual relationship with the establishment; or carrying out banking operations through an authorized representative without the owner’s knowledge. These practices also include opening multiple bank accounts for an establishment without a genuine business need or a clear link between them, which could be misused to channel funds. They also include conducting financial transactions, such as deposits, transfers, withdrawals, and purchases, involving individuals or business entities unrelated to the establishment’s commercial activities.

items.title: Azerbaijan signs Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh
items.title_zh: 阿塞拜疆签署2030年利雅得世博会参展合同
items.summary: RIYADH — Azerbaijan has officially signed its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, ushering in a new phase of preparations to develop its pavilion and finalize its programs and planned contributions.The official Expo 2030 Riyadh account stated that Azerbaijan’s participation will showcase contributions reflecting the richness of its culture, its achievements, and its aspirations for the future to millions of visitors.It added that Azerbaijan’s participation underscores the deep-rooted relations between the two countries while bringing greater diversity to the Expo 2030 Riyadh experience. The contract was signed by Chief Executive Officer of Expo 2030 Riyadh Talal Al-Marri and Assistant to the President of Azerbaijan Anar Alakbarov during a ceremony held in Baku, capital of Azerbaijan.The signing marks an important milestone in Azerbaijan’s participation journey, allowing it to move from planning into delivery of its presence at Expo 2030 Riyadh.Holding the ceremony in Baku reflects the longstanding friendship between the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as well as the importance Azerbaijan attaches to its participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh as a further opportunity to deepen cooperation between the two countries. Speaking on the occasion, Anar Alakbarov said that it is a great honor for Azerbaijan to sign its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh here in Baku. Azerbaijan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are bound by deep ties of friendship, mutual respect and close cooperation, which continue to grow across the political, economic, energy and cultural spheres. “Our participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh reflects the strength of this partnership and our support for the Kingdom in hosting this landmark global event. Through our pavilion, we look forward to sharing Azerbaijan’s rich heritage, culture and vision for the future with visitors from around the world, and to further strengthening the bonds between our nations,” he said.On his part, Talal Al-Marri said: “We are seeing growing momentum in international participation at Expo 2030 Riyadh, as more countries move from confirming their participation to actively planning their pavilions and visitor experiences. Azerbaijan’s signing of its Participation Contract marks another important milestone in this journey, and we look forward to working closely with our partners in Azerbaijan to support a participation that reflects their vision and ambitions, while offering visitors from around the world a distinctive experience. With every new Participation Contract signed, Expo 2030 Riyadh takes another step towards becoming a truly global gathering, bringing nations and people together to exchange ideas, strengthen collaboration, and forge meaningful partnerships that help shape our shared future.”Preparations for Expo 2030 Riyadh continue to advance on multiple fronts, with significant progress in both international participation and site development. More countries are moving towards formalizing their participation, while work on the ground continues at pace. With the Detailed Master Plan now complete, development activities are progressing across site preparation, major earthworks, enabling infrastructure and utility networks, laying the foundations for welcoming the world to Riyadh in 2030.Running from 1 October 2030 to 31 March 2031, Expo 2030 Riyadh will be among the most ambitious World Expos ever conceived with a 6 million square meter site that will bring together 197 Official Participants and is expected to welcome 42 million visits across 5 distinct districts.Held under the theme “Foresight for Tomorrow,” and hosted in Riyadh - a city of action and ambition - Expo 2030 Riyadh will provide a platform for participants to exchange ideas, shape solutions, and build partnerships that drive real impact, address global challenges, and unlock new opportunities. The World Expo will feature immersive cultural zones, daily activations, and AI-powered interactions, blending traditional Saudi hospitality with cutting-edge technology. Following the six-month event, the Expo site will evolve into a vibrant destination, continuing to attract visitors and contribute to Riyadh’s dynamic urban landscape.
